title: Native, Ark and TanStack keyboard comparison in an isolated workload

decision.recommendation: adopt-later: a minimal native policy correction in a separately assigned production slice; defer a hotkeys library

candidate_decisions.native-as-is: reject unchanged for the observed editor/sidebar/composition/modal workload; keep the retained as-is evidence
candidate_decisions.native: adopt-later, conditional on real integration, IME/accessibility evidence and owner agreement
candidate_decisions.ark: defer: passes the selected corrected vectors and Accounts byte screen but adds lifecycle/policy work without a demonstrated user benefit over corrected native; Web cost unproved
candidate_decisions.tanstack: reject 0.15.0/0.16.0 for this fixed workload: Accounts exceeds both byte screens and policy burden is not lower; do not infer a permanent rejection of future versions

decision.concrete_user_benefit: A writer can format bold or open an editor link without toggling the background sidebar or activating page search. Composition sentinel events and an open modal should not activate background accelerators. This is a plausible production benefit supported by imported-owner fixture failures, not yet observed user or real IME success.
decision.why_native: Every contender still needs the same application priority, composition, editable/widget, legacy cooperation and binding/help policy. Corrected native passes the same selected outcomes with one global adapter listener, no added dependency, no custom store lifecycle and the lowest measured Accounts bytes. Library parsing/sequences did not eliminate that policy.
decision.scope_limit: No production adoption, live route/listener, API operation, permission behavior, command owner, focus/retry owner, production manifest or lockfile was changed. No nested agents, upload, automatic landing, OS provisioning, shared-stack changes or Claude reservation.

budgets.origin: Manager judgment for a small accelerator; not measured limits. No tighter numerical route budget was found in the retained library report or the relevant performance/development documentation read; owner must confirm before production.

audit_recheck.method: Read retained library-research coordination and current keyboard owners before selecting imports; rechecked task goal -- status before reporting. No unlanded audit code was substituted into the baseline.
audit_recheck.authorization: Manager brief authorizes this isolated trial following G-2788 and audit-remediation mail:45070a9f-d154-459a-ad9a-3ae55fa655e1. Do not wait for G-2787/G-2792; their output is not claimed as proof.

fixture.logical_workload: Search, editor link, editor bold, sidebar, navigation/help. Three adapter globals plus two selected editor behaviors make 5; 45 unique inactive-product filler chords scale globals to 48 at 50. All fillers are enabled in the final rows. Other built-in Tiptap bindings remain fixed across contenders.
fixture.as_is_preservation: Actual unmodified SearchField, SidebarProvider and usePageKeys are imported for native-as-is. Count 50 does not create new owners there; its 50 timing is explicitly an unchanged-load control. Its diagnostic count is hardcoded3 after teardown and is not a measured leak.
fixture.coexistence_control: As-is deliberately has an independent legacy listener that ignores consumed/composition/modal policy; corrected native and both libraries give this same legacy listener the explicit shared guard plus active binding check. Count this cooperation cost for every corrected candidate. Duplicate legacy logs do not establish existing production duplication or a library benefit. Actual imported sidebar priority/IME failures also occur without a legacy action.
fixture.execution: Real adapters and actual Ark/Tiptap wrappers on pinned Vinext SSR, hydration and client navigation. Separate private copies of actual Web/Accounts use unchanged build configs with the fixture appended; no standalone fixture bundle is treated as route proof.
fixture.synthetic_vs_real: Deterministic vectors use KeyboardEvent dispatch (isTrusted=false). Browser-generated keyboard.type/Tab/Escape/ArrowDown verify selected editor/widget/focus outcomes. No real OS IME, AT, Mac/Windows or hardware timing observation.

policy_and_maintenance.count_unit: Guard family means one documented policy decision, not branches or LOC. Report shared costs once plus each candidate-specific adaptation. LOC is nonblank source lines including imports/comments/diagnostics, not a correctness or benefit score.
shared_guard_families: explicit modified-search exception in form controls
shared_policy_families: visible benign controls and action/focus observations

costs: Explicit exact key plus Control/Meta/Alt/Shift matching (five conditions), platform Mod mapping
G/H prefix state and one-second timeout
Current callback ref and add/remove one bubble keydown listener
native.scope: This is the proposed minimal native correction experiment, not a production migration.

costs: Bubble capture=false; disable library preventDefault/stopPropagation; enable form/contenteditable callbacks so shared guard owns decisions
Private stable store, public init(document)/destroy pairing, > sequence syntax conversion
Source-level lifecycle responsibility tied to document; environment replacement is unproved
ark.initial_counterexample: Without the explicit public init call, Strict Mode replay stopped search and allowed the cooperative legacy action instead. Retained previous-measurement/behavior-before-instrument-correction.json contains that failure. Public init resolved the executed case; no third-party patch or competing registry was required.

costs: Bubble capture=false; disable automatic preventDefault/stopPropagation; ignoreInputs=false to apply identical shared guard
Additional exact dependency closure and singleton manager diagnostics
Nested/exclusive scope API exists in this release but is not used to create a second focus owner. The shared existing modal/editor owner remains authoritative.

policy_and_maintenance.no_hidden_owner: The rows list is fixture binding/help metadata, not a second event registry. Each contender alone owns its adapter registrations. Existing Tiptap/widget focus/action owners remain common. No internal package patch was made.

keys-priority.observations: Native as-is editor bold toggled the actual imported sidebar with two preventDefault calls, while the editor also formatted text. The corrected native, Ark and TanStack adapters executed only the eligible owner in all 34 vectors, including editor link/bold, consumed targets, menu and modal priority.
gaps: No production command/API action or authority proof. Legacy duplicates in as-is are deliberately induced by an independent uncooperative fixture listener; candidate adapters all require its explicit policy cooperation.
Only selected modifier, character and G/H sequence vectors were tested; no claim for all product commands, scope graphs or browser defaults.

keys-ime.observations: Synthetic isComposing, keyCode229 with isComposing=false, Process, Unidentified, Dead and AltGraph-like Ctrl+Alt vectors were dispatched. Imported native SidebarProvider acted on composing and 229 Mod+B; SearchField acted on 229 Mod+K. Corrected candidates did not log or cancel globals on these vectors. The existing dialog remained open for synthetic 229 Escape.
gaps: All IME-related events are synthetic and isTrusted=false. No Chinese Pinyin/Japanese OS IME session, committed-text/caret proof, real candidate selection, Firefox or Safari execution.

keys-inputs.observations: Question-mark vectors in input, textarea, select, actual Tiptap and portal input produced no global help action. Menu owned its cancellation; combobox ArrowDown produced an active descendant. Browser typing after editor bold produced actual bold document marks.
gaps: Portal targets are covered; shadow roots, physical JIS layout, real AltGr/dead-key entry and RTL reader navigation are unproved. Synthetic character dispatch does not establish actual typed text.

keys-customization.observations: Corrected candidates supported disable, Mod+J remap, old-binding suppression, reset and G then H without cancelling the prefix. Help text and ARIA became Mod+J and Control+J. As-is owners expose no shared remap/disable hook, so their controls are not claimed to work.
gaps: Remap/disable/reset and G/H are in-memory fixture state. No persisted invalid settings, recorder, full product conflict namespace or localized recovery proof.
The invalid-remap capture selected the first status role (Sidebar open), so it does not prove rejection feedback. The whitelist is source evidence only; do not count that probe as a pass.

keys-access.observations: Actual editor toolbar link/bold, search/sidebar/help controls and focus outlines were visible. Existing dialog focus management was retained. This demonstrates benign action access in a fixture, not product API access, accessibility conformance or a complete journey.
gaps: Visible equivalents exist for the five benign actions; no actual rating/admin API permissions or touch/screen-reader journey. No assistive technology or automated accessibility audit was run.

Desktop and 390px/reduced-motion screenshots were viewed. The Japanese probe changes lang/font size and includes mixed Japanese manuscript content; it does not translate the English fixture or prove all eight UI locales.

keys-platform.observations: Actual React19.3.1/Vinext1.0.0-beta.13 SSR and client navigation ran for all adapters. Neutral SSR labels hydrated to Meta+K or Control+K under navigator overrides with no label-context console error. Accounts production route hydrated without pageerror for all three comparable adapters.
gaps: Linux headless Chromium only. MacIntel/Win32/Linux navigator overrides test ARIA strings, not OS input or reserved shortcuts.

Development optimizer emitted 504 Outdated Optimize Dep / dynamic import recovery warnings for every adapter. No hydration mismatch or pageerror was recorded; initial dev recovery is a partial compatibility result, not a clean hydration certification. Web production preview stream could not be read within 3 seconds.

keys-lifecycle.observations: Five mount/unmount cycles returned to six shared document/window key listeners for every adapter, with zero post-unmount actions/cancellations. Corrected adapters had zero registered globals after unmount. Ark needed explicit public store.init({target:document}) paired with destroy to survive Strict Mode; after that, Strict Mode and navigation ran one action.
gaps: HMR, document/environment replacement, permission changes, delayed sequences across focus/scope changes and authenticated cross-request isolation were not exercised.
Two concurrent SSR responses were 200 with neutral labels and no browser-global exception. This is limited smoke evidence, not proof of zero cross-request user state.

keys-cost.observations: Accounts native/Ark/TanStack production routes yielded all loaded JS/CSS response sizes and 360 samples per 5/50 workload. Ark passed that route byte screen; TanStack exceeded both byte limits. Each production p95 was <=0.5 ms on this device and passed the fixed latency screen. Web remains unproved.
gaps: Web builds passed but /en/discover streamed response reading timed out; loaded Web chunks and route latency are unavailable. No substitution of emitted total files or tarball bytes.

The comparable native byte baseline is the corrected native adapter in the same private fixture and unchanged production route, not an as-is production deployment or a production correction implementation.
The full common editor/widget fixture is intentionally heavy. Totals describe this workload, not a minimal accelerator, real user payload or cold/warm network timings.

focus-return.observations: All four fixtures returned focus to modal-trigger after close settled. Nested initial focus, containment and parent survival were true; pending Escape and synthetic 229 Escape preserved the dialog. An earlier unsettled snapshot incorrectly read modal-input; retained raw captures show that harness correction.
gaps: Existing dialog owner passed settled initial/contained focus, pending Escape, nested close, return to a surviving trigger and synthetic 229 Escape.
Removal of the trigger, focus fallback, touch close, menu/editor-origin nesting, real IME Escape and screen-reader behavior remain unproved.

web.reason: All builds completed. Preview logged GET 200 but response.text exceeded the 3-second AbortSignal timeout before chunk collection. The cause of the incomplete stream is not isolated. Do not treat a 200 header, emitted files or Accounts sizes as Web cost proof.

production_route_cost.latency_method: Same device/browser and fixture; count5 then50; 3 batches x120 synchronous keydown/keyup samples. Interval performance.now before dispatch to benign action-log timestamp, not render/paint or hardware input. Browser timer resolution approximately0.1ms; zero samples reflect quantization. No smoothing or discarded outliers; all360 expected production search actions were present for each measured workload.
production_route_cost.latency_screen: All measured Accounts p95 values <=0.5ms, <=8ms and <=native p95+1ms. Web and real-input latency remain unproved.
production_route_cost.transitive_proof: Loaded chunk records include raw/gzip/Brotli/hash for every observed script/stylesheet and emitted module maps for client/server/SSR. Static package/license closure is separate from loaded route cost.

ark.observation: Official Ark docs still label Hotkeys preview. Installed hotkeys entry depends on Zag hotkeys/dom-query; being present in yarn.lock does not make its route bytes free.

tanstack.maturity: Exact-commit README still describes the library as beta; GitHub release prerelease=false does not establish stable integration.

release_and_license_refresh.license_observation: All13 inventoried exact runtime/type closure entries declare MIT and have an installed license notice whose hash is retained. Ark umbrella manifest lists unrelated widgets; only its hotkeys entry closure is recursively inventoried here. Actual route module maps retain the full bundled transitive graph. This is package inventory, not legal clearance.
release_and_license_refresh.sandbox: Yarn4.18.0, enableScripts=false; exact React/core TanStack packages exempted only inside the private trial from the1440-minute age quarantine. No silent upgrade or production dependency change.

rendered_review.method: Repository screenshot review procedure, opt-in Playwright fallback in the explicit browser harness; available browser MCP was not present. Actual PNGs were opened with view_image.
findings: Common desktop and narrow fixture content remained readable with no measured horizontal overflow at390px; editor toolbar wrapped. Focus outline visible on search and nested-modal invoker.
Existing modal was visibly above the dimmed background and retained its input/close controls.
The private Accounts appended fixture has plain controls with sparse spacing because no research-only CSS was injected into the production route. It is measurement UI, not production design approval.
limits: No Storybook suite, pixel baseline, all-locale translation review, touch input, forced-colors/contrast audit or real assistive technology proof.

follow_ups.owner: Product-completion manager with Web shell, Accounts keyboard and shared UI owners
follow_ups.smallest_question: Assign a production slice for shared eligibility policy in existing native owners: does editor Mod+B stop toggling the sidebar, and do 229/modal events leave background actions alone, with legacy cooperation explicit?
follow_ups.decision_changed_by: A production integration showing those failures fixed with no greater policy burden and no new command/focus owner supports native adoption after remaining gates. Fixture logs alone do not.

follow_ups.owner: Web runtime/QA owner under host admission
follow_ups.smallest_question: Why does the built /en/discover response stream not complete within the fixture timeout, and can one healthy private preview yield loaded-chunk/latency evidence for the three unchanged adapters?
follow_ups.decision_changed_by: Both gzip/Brotli route deltas and latency meeting the fixed or tighter owner budget can close cost; missing evidence keeps Ark deferred and any adoption blocked.

follow_ups.owner: Keyboard/accessibility owner on already available target devices
follow_ups.smallest_question: Run real Pinyin/Japanese candidate Enter/Escape/arrows and actual screen-reader/keyboard/touch actions with the production native correction, then the same candidate only if it still offers a concrete benefit.
follow_ups.decision_changed_by: Lost text/caret, unintended action/dismissal or AT conflict rejects the proposed behavior; complete real-device evidence is required for adoption.

follow_ups.smallest_question: When a dialog invoker is removed, does close restore focus to a logical surviving successor, including composition Escape and nested menu/editor origins?
follow_ups.decision_changed_by: Focus loss or double dismissal needs a separately owned wrapper fix, not another focus package.

follow_ups.owner: Product-completion manager with G-2787 journey evidence and G-2782 review
follow_ups.smallest_question: Does any observed user journey need a registry/scope feature that the small native correction cannot supply with equal or lower policy burden?
follow_ups.decision_changed_by: Only a concrete failed workload reopens Ark or a new exact TanStack release; byte reduction alone without a user/policy benefit does not justify adding the dependency.

research_refresh_policy.owner: Product-completion manager assigns the next smallest question to current domain owners; this report creates no watcher or permanent research owner.
triggers: Relevant React, Vinext, Ark or Tiptap upgrade: rerun SSR/hydration/navigation, lifecycle and the affected behavior/cost rows.
New or changed hotkeys scope/event/lifecycle API: inspect exact release/license/closure and repeat only the workload whose policy might shrink.
Observed priority, real IME or accessibility failure: reopen the failing invariant on all in-scope keyboard owners.
G-2787 journey evidence, G-2782 review or actual user/AT observations: refine visible equivalents and real integration acceptance.
Before any install/adoption, refresh exact releases, licenses, notices and dependency closure; preserve this comparison rather than silently replacing pins.
research_refresh_policy.other_libraries: Reopen URL, list, form, motion or other libraries only for a concrete failed workload; no static shortlist refresh.
research_refresh_policy.stop_rule: One useful comparison is complete. Web cost, real-device and remaining integration gaps become explicit follow-ups; no OS/shared-stack provisioning, watcher, Claude reservation or automatic production adoption.
